## 📌 Introduction After creating your Telegram bot, it's time to bring it to life! In this guide, you will learn exactly how to make your bot respond and work — **no coding experience needed**, just your phone and a little patience. Let's get started! 😀 --- > ⚠️ **Important:** If you haven't created your Telegram bot yet, we strongly recommend reading this guide first 👇

How to Create a Telegram Bot — Complete Guide

By mohammadabuhanifmia
--- ## ✅ Already have your bot? Great! Follow the steps below 👇 --- ## 📋 Steps --- ### ✅ Step 1 — Download & Install Termux Before we begin, we need to install **Termux** — a powerful terminal app that lets you run Linux-style commands directly on your Android phone. > ⚠️ **Important:** You **must** download Termux from **F-Droid**, not from the Google Play Store. The Play Store version is outdated and may not work correctly. Visit the F-Droid website: [click here to visit F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/) **Or download F-Droid directly below 👇**

Download F-Droid

Download (12.43 MB)
After installing F-Droid, open it and search for **`Termux`** in the search bar. Select the app named exactly **"Terminal emulation with packages — Termux"**, then tap **Install**. When prompted, allow F-Droid to install apps from unknown sources by following this path:
Required Permission:

To allow F-Droid to install and update apps, you need to enable the installation permission in your device settings by following this path:

⚙️Settings
›
Apps
›
Special app access
›
Install unknown apps
›
Enable F-Droid
💡 Quick Tip:

When you download your first app, F-Droid will show a prompt that takes you directly to this settings screen automatically.

--- ### ✅ Step 2 — Set Up Termux Open the **Termux** app. You will see a black terminal screen — don't worry, this is completely normal! Now run the following commands **one by one**: #### 🔄 First — Update all packages: ```bash pkg update && pkg upgrade -y ``` > 📝 **Note:** During this process you may be asked questions in the terminal. Simply type `y` and press **Enter** each time to confirm. --- #### 📂 Then — Grant Termux access to your phone storage: ```bash termux-setup-storage ``` A popup will appear asking for permission — tap **"Allow"** to grant Termux access to your phone's storage. --- #### 🐍 Then — Install Python: ```bash pkg install python -y ``` > 💡 Python is the programming language we will use to power your bot. --- ### ✅ Step 3 — Create Your Bot Project Folder Now let's organize everything properly by creating a dedicated folder for your bot. **Create a new folder named `mybot`:** ```bash mkdir mybot ``` **Navigate into that folder:** ```bash cd mybot ``` --- ### ✅ Step 4 — Install the Nano Text Editor We need **Nano** — a simple in-terminal text editor — to create and write your bot's code file. ```bash pkg install nano -y ``` --- ### ✅ Step 5 — Create the Bot Script File Now create your bot's Python file using Nano: ```bash nano bot.py ``` You will see a blank black editor screen. This is where you will paste your bot's code. **Copy the example code below:** ```python import telebot # Replace with your actual Telegram Bot Token from @BotFather TOKEN = 'YOUR_BOT_TOKEN_HERE' bot = telebot.TeleBot(TOKEN) @bot.message_handler(commands=['start']) def send_welcome(message): bot.reply_to(message, "Hello! This bot is running 100% from Termux! 🚀") @bot.message_handler(func=lambda message: True) def echo_all(message): bot.reply_to(message, f"You said: {message.text}") print("Bot is starting...") bot.infinity_polling() ``` > ⚠️ **Important:** Replace `YOUR_BOT_TOKEN_HERE` with the **secret API token** you received from **@BotFather**. To find it, go to Telegram → open **@BotFather** → scroll to the success message → copy your token. After replacing the token, your final code should look like this: ```python import telebot TOKEN = '893****02:AA*r13H_zh*******CXlWlr*j7a1i4***wjQ' bot = telebot.TeleBot(TOKEN) @bot.message_handler(commands=['start']) def send_welcome(message): bot.reply_to(message, "Hello! This bot is running 100% from Termux! 🚀") @bot.message_handler(func=lambda message: True) def echo_all(message): bot.reply_to(message, f"You said: {message.text}") print("Bot is starting...") bot.infinity_polling() ``` Now go back to **Termux**, tap and hold inside the terminal, and select **"Paste"** to paste the code into the editor. **To save and exit the Nano editor:** | Action | Keys | |--------|------| | Save the file | Press `CTRL` + `O`, then press `Enter` | | Exit the editor | Press `CTRL` + `X` | --- ### ✅ Step 6 — Install the Bot Library Before running your bot, install the required Python library: ```bash pip install pyTelegramBotAPI ``` --- ### ✅ Step 7 — Run Your Bot! Now start your bot with this command: ```bash python bot.py ``` If everything is set up correctly, you will see this message in Termux: ``` Bot is starting... ``` 🎉 **That means your bot is now live and working!** --- ### ✅ Step 8 — Test Your Bot Go back to **Telegram** → open **@BotFather** → scroll to your bot's success message. You will see something like: > 💬 *"Done! Congratulations on your new bot. You will find it at* `t.me/cocahotel_bot`*. You can now add a description, about section and profile picture for your bot..."* > — **@BotFather** Tap the link (e.g. `t.me/cocahotel_bot`) to open your bot, then press the **"Start"** button. Your bot will instantly reply with: > 💬 *"Hello! This bot is running 100% from Termux! 🚀"* > — **Your Bot** ✅ --- ## 🔋 Keep Your Bot Running in the Background To prevent your bot from stopping when Termux goes to sleep, do the following: Pull down your **notification panel** → find the **Termux notification** → tap **"Acquire Wakelock"** to keep Termux running in the background at all times. --- ## 🎉 Congratulations! Your Bot Is Now Fully Alive! You have successfully: - ✅ Installed Termux and Python - ✅ Created a bot script - ✅ Connected it to your Telegram bot token - ✅ Launched and tested your bot - ✅ Kept it running in the background --- ## 🛠️ Helpful Terminal Commands Use these powerful commands to manage and maintain your bot like a pro: | # | Command | Description | |---|---------|-------------| | 1 | `pkill -f python` | **Force-kill all Python processes** — Stops every hidden or frozen Python process on your phone. Run this before restarting your bot. | | 2 | `find . -type d -name "__pycache__" -exec rm -r {} +` | **Clear Python cache** — Deletes all compiled temporary files so your script reloads completely clean. | | 3 | `pkg clean && apt autoremove -y` | **Clear Termux system trash** — Removes downloaded installation files and orphaned packages to free up storage. | | 4 | `history -c && clear` | **Wipe terminal screen & history** — Clears your screen buffer and resets command memory so Termux runs smoother. | --- > 💡 **What's Next?** > Now that your bot is live, you can start customizing it — add commands, keyboards, databases, and much more using the [Telegram Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api). The possibilities are endless! 🚀
